title: Alphabet Sheds Half a Trillion in Market Value in Stock's Worst Day Ever
summary: Alphabet shares suffered their steepest one-day drop on record after quarterly results, erasing roughly half a trillion dollars of market value. Investor discontent centered on slowing search revenue growth (12%, from 17% a quarter earlier) and negative free cash flow of about $9.1 billion, even as Google Cloud revenue grew 103%. The reaction highlights tensions in Alphabet's transition from search engine to AI hyperscaler.

title: Alphabet Still Has the Ingredients to Win in an AI Pullback
summary: A WSJ analysis argues that Alphabet is no longer loved by investors despite a broad set of advantages across cloud, chips, models and distribution. It frames the company as relatively well positioned if enthusiasm for AI spending cools.

title: Amazon Earnings Miss Wall Street Estimates Despite Highest Cloud Growth in Five Years
summary: Amazon reported third-quarter results in which AWS revenue came in above expectations and cloud growth hit its fastest pace in five years, with net profit topping $20 billion. Overall earnings nonetheless missed Wall Street estimates.

title: Canada to Take Equity Stake in AI Firm Cohere
summary: Canada's government will take an equity stake in Cohere, committing up to $1.6 billion as the company raises about $7 billion at a reported $35.7 billion valuation. Nvidia, Germany's Schwarz Group and telecom firm BCE are among those with commitments to the round.

title: AI Is Almost the Easy Part. Everything Else Is Hard
summary: Microsoft and Google earnings show AI demand outrunning capacity, with Google Cloud up 103% and Azure up 48%, but the harder challenges are business-model and operating-model disruption. Google's search growth slowed as AI Mode monetizes at lower rates, ServiceNow fell 14% on AI fears, and Microsoft has offered buyouts to about 60,000 employees while rebuilding how work gets done.

title: Samsung Posts Fourth Straight Quarter of Record Earnings as AI Keeps Memory Chips Scarce
summary: Samsung Electronics reported a fourth consecutive record quarter as AI demand kept memory chips in short supply, with next year's supply already sold out and tightness expected through 2028. Shares still fell more than 5% as results missed lofty expectations amid concerns about AI infrastructure spending.

title: Google Releases Gemini 4 Carbon, Topping Intelligence Index Ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra
summary: Google launched Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier model, citing significant gains in coding, agentic tasks and cybersecurity. It ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0), ahead of Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra.

title: Incident Response Overload: Hacked Companies Have to Stand in Line for Help
summary: Incident-response providers including Palo Alto Networks, Sophos, MoxFive and Resilience report record volumes of customer requests as fast-moving threats strain emergency-response capacity. A Lightspeed and Wakefield survey also found 88% of CISOs let AI agents take some security response actions with no human in the loop.

title: 'Skeptical' Lawyers Highlight Growing Pains of AI Agents
summary: White & Case is gradually rolling out Legora's newer AI agent because many lawyers are hesitant, even though 90% of the firm's staff already use Legora products to some extent. Legora, valued around $9 billion, says it has passed $200 million in annualized recurring revenue, while client pressure for efficiency is what is ultimately forcing adoption.

title: Sebastian Thrun Raises $130 Million for AI Engineering Startup Dulo
summary: Sebastian Thrun and co-founder Adrian Aoun's new startup Dulo, building AI models for engineering, closed a $130 million seed round. Backers reportedly include Eric Schmidt, John Doerr, DST Global, Construct Capital and Lowercarbon Capital.

title: OpenAI's Astra Model Becomes Top Distillation Target for China's AI Labs
summary: DeepSeek and Moonshot AI reportedly relied heavily on outputs from OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to train their latest models, a practice known as distillation. It remains one of the biggest contributors to progress in Chinese open-weight models despite criticism from OpenAI and Anthropic.

title: Everyone's Using AI But Divisions Are Growing: WTF Highlights
summary: Takeaways from The Information's WTF Summit suggest AI adoption is now dividing companies and investors. Goldman Sachs investment banking co-head Kim Posnett said investors are favoring companies that control model training, chips and data centers, describing a repositioning and differentiation across the AI trade rather than a change in sentiment.

title: T-Mobile US CEO Rules Out SpaceX MVNO Deal
summary: T-Mobile US CEO Srini Gopalan told analysts on the Q3 earnings call that he sees no reason for an MVNO arrangement with SpaceX. The comments follow similar skepticism from Verizon's CEO about SpaceX's threat to carriers.

title: Apple Adds Touchscreen MacBook Pro Starting at $2,899
summary: Apple unveiled its first touchscreen MacBook Pro after years of resisting the feature, as part of a wave of product announcements under CEO John Ternus. It starts at $2,899, a $900 premium over the $1,999 non-touchscreen model.

title: Big Tech Earnings Week Ends in Selloff, but Cloud Businesses Outperform
summary: Amazon and Intel fell sharply in premarket trading after Thursday earnings, and Alphabet's slide continued after a 13% one-day drop that erased roughly $500 billion in market value. Cloud was the bright spot: AWS revenue reached $46 billion (up 39%), Azure grew 48% and Google Cloud grew 103%, driven by AI demand. Investors remain focused on whether heavy AI spending will produce sufficient returns.

title: Enterprise AI Is on the Ballot Too
summary: Ahead of next week's midterms, tech policy debates on frontier-model limits, data center build-outs, state AI laws and job protections could still reshape how CIOs deploy AI. A Cato Institute fellow warns that rules aimed at AI companies will spill over to other industries, including through age-verification requirements for chatbots, while a state-level patchwork complicates enterprise deployment. Proposals to restrict AI-driven job elimination are also gaining political traction.

title: Mistral Releases Open-Weight Model 'Le Chonk' (Mistral Large 4)
summary: Mistral released Mistral Large 4, which it calls the best open-weight model for coding and cybersecurity. Booz Allen Hamilton said its testing found vulnerability-detection recall comparable to other frontier cyber models at a compelling cost. The model was trained on 3,800 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs in Europe, and Mistral's valuation recently exceeded $24 billion after a Samsung-led round.

title: Hackers Steal Roughly $6.3 Billion from Binance in Possible Record Crypto Heist
summary: Binance halted transactions after attackers took roughly $6.3 billion, which could be the largest crypto theft on record. The exchange said the breach may have stemmed from a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop that allowed unauthorized withdrawals, and some security researchers suspect a North Korean group. Separately, about $2.6 million was drained from Polymarket accounts through a third-party monitoring tool.

title: Singapore Data-Center Executive Close to Nvidia CEO Suspected of Passing Information to China
summary: Officials in the U.S., Singapore and Taiwan suspect Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who worked with Nvidia on Asian data centers, has been a source for Chinese intelligence. U.S. officials reportedly concluded last year that she was sharing information with Beijing. Megaspeed is also the subject of a Justice Department probe into whether it diverted Nvidia chips to China in violation of export controls.

title: Amazon Shrugs Off Outside Shopping Agents and Touts Its Own
summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said external shopping agents are not meaningfully affecting Amazon Ads, while saying more than 400 million customers used Alexa for Shopping in the past year, with interactions up 570% and 50% higher spend per order. Amazon ad revenue growth slowed to 12% ex-currency, partly due to Prime Day moving to June, and it expects high-teens growth in the fourth quarter. Amazon has blocked Meta's Muse agent and is fighting Perplexity's shopping agent in court.

title: Generali Agrees to Roughly $727 Million, 20-Year Naming Deal for AC Milan and Inter Stadium
summary: Insurer Generali will pay 650 million euros over 20 years to name the new Milan stadium shared by AC Milan and Inter 'Generali Stadium', according to a person close to the deal. A sponsorship research executive said it would be one of the largest stadium naming-rights deals worldwide, for context a crypto brokerage paid $700 million in 2021 for the Los Angeles arena now called Crypto.com Arena. Construction is expected to begin in 2028 with first matches in the 2031-32 season.

title: Legal AI Startup Crosby Bids for Assets of Fallen Law Firm Weil Gotshal
summary: Crosby, a two-year-old startup whose lawyers use AI for contract review and other legal work, submitted a letter of intent to buy some assets of Weil, Gotshal & Manges after the firm decided to wind down. The bid covers internal data, the trademark and the brand, and Crosby hopes to hire some of Weil's 1,200 lawyers. Terms were not disclosed.

title: An Anthropic Windfall Could Await State Pension Funds
summary: The Information's analysis finds that Anthropic's planned IPO is set to produce cash payouts for state pension plans in California, Massachusetts and other states that hold stakes in the company. The piece looks at how public retirement systems stand to benefit from the AI lab's public listing.

title: Encryption Under Siege? OpenAI, Anthropic Disprove Key Cryptography Theorem
summary: Encryption researchers are growing uneasy after recent findings by Anthropic and OpenAI that disproved a key cryptography theorem. The report examines what the results could mean for the security assumptions underpinning modern encryption.

title: Global Smartphone Shipments Fall 20% in Q3 to Lowest Level in More Than a Decade
summary: Omdia reported that global smartphone shipments fell 20% year on year to 254.7 million units in the third quarter, the lowest Q3 volume in over ten years.

title: Deutsche Telekom Cools on Merger With T-Mobile US
summary: A Deutsche Telekom plan to merge with its subsidiary T-Mobile US reportedly hit an obstacle, and the German operator decided not to make a formal offer for now.

title: FCC Proposes Auction of 25MHz of Spectrum for Satellite D2D and Terrestrial Networks
summary: The U.S. FCC proposed auctioning 25MHz of spectrum for satellite direct-to-device services and terrestrial wireless networks. Separately, it floated rules to bar providers on a national-security threat list from directly accessing U.S. phone numbers for VoIP calls, drawing criticism from Chinese authorities.

title: Orange Cyberdefense Partners With Mistral AI on Security Services
summary: Orange Cyberdefense struck a partnership with Mistral AI to build services on a specialised version of Mistral's latest large language model, as European companies seek stronger defences against automated cyber threats.

title: OpenAI Raises Less Than Half of $30 Billion Target in Latest Round
summary: OpenAI's latest funding round values the ChatGPT maker at $1.25 trillion, below the $1.4 trillion it had been targeting. The round raised less than half of the $30 billion goal, indicating investor resistance to the higher price.

title: The Smartest People in AI Believe This Is the World's Most Important Chart
summary: WSJ reports that AI systems are beginning to build better AI, a self-improvement loop that is speeding up research and development. The trend, tracked in a chart tied to Anthropic's recursive self-improvement work, is alarming many in the field.

title: The New Bottleneck in America's AI Build-Out: A Shortage of Cheap Money
summary: Lenders and investors are becoming choosier about AI infrastructure bets and demanding stricter terms as the build-out enters a new phase. Access to inexpensive capital, rather than chips, is emerging as a constraint on further expansion.

title: Exclusive: Meta Built Humanoid Prototype With Chinese Startup To Ramp Up Robotics Push
summary: Meta has built a roughly 106-pound prototype humanoid, known internally as Max, with Chinese robotics company Fourier in about three months, and is already working on a second version. The effort is aimed at developing robots for people's homes, though no launch target has been set, according to people familiar with the work.

title: Anthropic's S-1 Takeaways: From Giant Compute Commitments to Complex Lock-Ups
summary: The Information distills the main points from Anthropic's newly public S-1 filing, including its very large compute commitments and a complicated structure of share lock-ups. Anthropic is reportedly targeting a Nasdaq debut the week of Nov. 16.

title: Anthropic's Seven Co-Founders Want Palantir-Style Voting Control After IPO
summary: Anthropic's seven co-founders are seeking Palantir-style voting control once the company is public, and the S-1 now spells out how the arrangement would work. The Information also notes that Anthropic matches employee charity donations with company stock, a cost to shareholders that could grow after the IPO.

title: OpenAI Offers Deep Discounts to Win Over Anthropic's Customers
summary: OpenAI is offering steep discounts to win Anthropic's customers, and several startups have already shifted spending, according to The Information. Anthropic's high margins left the opening, and whether it can win those customers back remains open.

title: Anthropic's Slowing Growth Weighs on IPO Valuation Talk
summary: Investors who saw Anthropic's latest quarter in a private meeting are reportedly rethinking the valuation bankers have floated, citing slowing growth. The Information separately argues the S-1 shows Anthropic running its models far more efficiently than a year ago, which may force skeptics to rethink the margin math.
